sources.entry: DisplayLatch - Keeps external monitors connected after sleep and restart, with DDC brightness, resolution and disconnect-without-unplugging controls. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/Hitesh-Sisara/DisplayLatch) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.name: DisplayLatch
summary.one_liner: DisplayLatch is a free, open-source macOS menu-bar app that changes external monitor brightness over DDC/CI, controls resolution, and restores monitors that stay black after sleep.
keywords: control external monitor brightness on mac
use_cases: Dimming external monitors at night without a grey overlay
Adjusting brightness of all screens with one slider
Fixing an external monitor that stays black after sleep or restart
Temporarily turning off a monitor for a call or game without unplugging
Switching display resolution for a screen share
Scripting brightness changes from Terminal, Shortcuts or cron
summary.what_it_does: DisplayLatch is a menu-bar app for macOS that sends DDC/CI commands to external monitors so their real backlight brightness changes, with a slider for all displays (including the built-in screen) plus per-monitor sliders. It detects monitors that are attached but kept off the desktop after sleep or restart and puts them back in their previous arrangement, checking after display changes, after wake, and every 20 seconds. It can disconnect a display from the desktop without unplugging it, and it offers a resolution switcher listing every mode macOS provides per display. It also includes a command-line tool (displaylatch list, brightness, resolution, disconnect, fix) for scripting.
notable: Real DDC/CI backlight brightness control instead of a software overlay, with one slider for all screens
Auto-restores monitors left black after sleep, keeping their arrangement position
Disconnect a display without unplugging, and a command-line tool
Native Swift/SwiftUI app, about 1.5 MB, no account or telemetry
caveats: Requires Apple silicon Mac running macOS 14 Sonoma or newer, per the FAQ
Brightness depends on monitors supporting DDC/CI; the built-in HDMI port on M1 Macs and base M2 Mac mini does not pass DDC
Uses private macOS display functions looked up at runtime, so an OS update could disable individual features
